items.name: Mount Bromo
items.summary: Mount Bromo is located within the Tengger Caldera, East Java — straddling Probolinggo, Malang, Pasuruan, and Lumajang regencies, approximately 2–3 hours from Surabaya's Juanda Airport. At 2,329 m above sea level, it is an active volcano famous for its sunrise views across the Sea of Sand (Lautan Pasir). A 4WD jeep crosses the caldera floor to the viewpoint; crater rim access is on foot.
items.highlight: Sunrise over Tengger Caldera and sacred Hindu ceremonies
items.description:
Mount Bromo, standing at 2,
329 meters, is one of the most iconic volcanoes in Indonesia and the most famous in East Java. It is located within the massive Tengger Caldera, surrounded by the Sea of Sand (Lautan Pasir). The name 'Bromo' is derived from the Javanese pronunciation of Brahma, the Hindu creator god.

The volcano is part of the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park and is sacred to the Tenggerese people, who are the descendants of the Majapahit empire. Every year, the Tenggerese hold the Yadnya Kasada ceremony where offerings are thrown into the crater to honor the mountain gods.

The sunrise view from viewpoints like Penanjakan or Kingkong Hill is considered one of the most spectacular in Southeast Asia, with Mount Semeru occasionally erupting in the background. The experience represents the perfect harmony between natural wonder and living culture.

keyInfo.permit_details: National Park entry fee: Foreign tourists IDR 220,000 (weekdays), IDR 320,000 (weekends). Domestic: IDR 25,000-50,000. JVTO includes all permits.
keyInfo.physical_requirements: Moderate physical condition required. The main challenge is the 250-step staircase to the crater rim. Suitable for most fitness levels with proper pacing.

items.name: Ijen Crater
items.summary: Kawah Ijen is located in Banyuwangi Regency, East Java, Indonesia — approximately 3 hours by car from Banyuwangi city and 5–6 hours from Surabaya (Juanda Airport). It is the world's largest acidic crater lake and one of only two places where SO₂ combustion at high temperature occurs. Entry requires a BBKSDA health certificate; all JVTO Ijen packages include mandatory in-hotel health screening by a licensed physician.
items.description:
Mount Ijen is a composite volcano located in the Banyuwangi Regency of East Java, Indonesia. It is part of the Ijen Volcano Complex, a group of stratovolcanoes inside a larger caldera. Ijen is famous for its turquoise-colored acidic crater lake, which is the largest of its kind in the world.

The volcano is most famous for the electric-blue flame that issues from cracks in the volcano at night. The flames are the result of combustion of sulfuric gases that emerge from the volcano at high pressure and temperature. The sulfuric combustion is visible only in darkness, making the midnight trek a unique experience.

Local sulfur miners work in extreme conditions, carrying heavy loads of sulfur up the steep crater walls. Their resilience and the stunning natural phenomena make Ijen one of Java's most compelling destinations.

keyInfo.permit_details: Available at Paltuding entry gate. Foreign tourists: IDR 100,000 (weekdays), IDR 150,000 (weekends). Domestic: IDR 5,000-15,000.
keyInfo.physical_requirements: Good physical condition required for steep ascent and high altitude. Not recommended for people with respiratory or heart conditions.

items.name: Madakaripura Waterfall
items.summary: A sacred 200-meter canyon waterfall believed to be the final meditation site of Gajah Mada, symbolizing loyalty and unity from the Majapahit legacy.
items.highlight: Sacred 200-meter canyon waterfall and Gajah Mada's meditation site
items.description:
Madakaripura Waterfall is a spectacular 200-meter tall waterfall located in a deep canyon in Probolinggo Regency, East Java. The name 'Madakaripura' translates to 'the place that is eternally kept or preserved,' reflecting its significance as a spiritual sanctuary.

This waterfall holds immense historical importance as it is believed to be the final meditation site of Gajah Mada, the legendary prime minister of the Majapahit Empire who swore the famous Palapa Oath to unite the Indonesian archipelago. The waterfall cascades down sheer cliff walls, creating a mystical atmosphere with constant mist and occasional rainbows when sunlight penetrates the canyon between 08:30–09:30 AM.

The site represents the element of Water in Javanese cosmology - symbolizing cleansing, renewal, and the flow of devotion that never ends.

keyInfo.permit_details: Local entry ticket required: IDR 15,000-25,000 per person. JVTO includes all entrance fees.
keyInfo.physical_requirements: Moderate fitness required for river trekking and navigating slippery surfaces. Must be comfortable walking in water and on uneven terrain.

items.name: Tumpak Sewu Waterfall
items.summary: A multi-stream semicircular waterfall formed by Mount Semeru's volcanic erosion, known for its canyon trail and panoramic viewpoint with Semeru backdrop.
items.highlight: Thousand-stream waterfall curtain with Mount Semeru backdrop
items.description:
Tumpak Sewu, which translates to 'A Thousand Waterfalls' in Javanese, is one of Indonesia's most spectacular waterfall formations. Located on the border between Lumajang and Malang regencies, this horseshoe-shaped waterfall cascades down a volcanic cliff face in hundreds of individual streams, creating a breathtaking natural curtain of water.

The waterfall is fed by the Glidik River, which originates from the slopes of Mount Semeru, Java's highest and most active volcano. The panoramic viewpoint offers a stunning perspective with Semeru often visible in the background, especially during sunrise. The descent to the waterfall base involves navigating bamboo ladders, ropes, and rocky paths, making it an adventurous experience.

Locals refer to Tumpak Sewu as 'Semeru's Breath,' representing the continuous flow of life from the volcano to the earth below.

keyInfo.permit_details: Entry fee: IDR 20,000-30,000 per person. Additional guide fee for canyon descent. JVTO includes all fees.
keyInfo.physical_requirements: Excellent physical condition required. Must be comfortable with heights, steep descents, and using ropes. Not recommended for people with mobility issues, fear of heights, or heart conditions.

items.name: Papuma Beach
items.summary: Beautiful white sand beach with unique rock formations and clear turquoise waters in Jember, East Java
items.highlight: White sand beach with turquoise waters and unique rock formations
items.description:
Papuma Beach, located in Jember Regency of East Java, is renowned for its stunning white sand and crystal-clear turquoise waters. The name 'Papuma' is an acronym from 'Pasir Putih Malikan' which means Malikan's White Sand. The beach features unique rock formations scattered along the coastline and offers panoramic views from nearby hilltops.

Unlike many other beaches in East Java, Papuma boasts fine white sand and relatively calm waters during the dry season. The beach is surrounded by lush green hills and features several small islands that can be reached during low tide. While swimming is limited due to strong Indian Ocean currents, the beach offers excellent opportunities for photography, relaxation, and enjoying spectacular sunsets.

The combination of white sand, turquoise waters, and unique geological formations makes Papuma one of East Java's most picturesque coastal destinations.

keyInfo.permit_details: Entrance fee: IDR 40,000 per person included in package.
keyInfo.physical_requirements: Minimal physical requirements. Suitable for all ages and fitness levels. Basic mobility required for beach access.
